Patrick — adding the infra/ops perspective below. I kept this intentionally pragmatic for your reviewers; happy to expand any section.

1) Hardware & kernel-level isolation- We schedule models onto Dedicated GPU nodes that are configured in GPU-exclusive mode (NVIDIA MIG where available, or exclusive compute mode otherwise). That prevents multiple CUDA contexts from being created by independent tenants on the same GPU instance.
- Each inference worker runs in its own container with minimal host privileges; we enforce strong Linux namespaces, seccomp filters, and cgroups (CPU/memory/io) so processes cannot inspect or access other processes' address spaces.

2) KV cache and memory handling- The runtime's KV cache is an in-process structure keyed by request session and model instance. For Dedicated deployments we allocate KV cache memory per-tenant process; there is no shared global cache across tenants on the same host.
- Cache entries are held in volatile memory only. We do not swap KV shards to host disk; our configuration disables persisting model KV to disk for Hosted Dedicated nodes.
- On eviction (e.g., when a tenant exceeds throttles or a noisy neighbor is detected) the runtime will: (a) immediately revoke further scheduling to the offending worker, (b) gracefully flush KV for the affected process, and (c) if SLOs are endangered, surface a routing decision to the Smart Router to move new requests to warm spare capacity or a lower-cost fallback model variant. Eviction is observable in telemetry and we retain short-lived audit traces (request ids + event markers) for troubleshooting.

3) Noisy neighbor detection & mitigation- Metrics-based detectors watch P99 latency, GPU utilization, memory growth, and kernel-level OOM signals. When thresholds are violated we apply QoS limits at the cgroup level (CPU shares, oom_score_adj), throttle batching, and optionally isolate the process to a dedicated core set. If the noisy behavior persists we trigger automated migration to reserved spare capacity and notify the customer and ops.

4) Cryptographic and key isolation- For Hosted customers keys are stored in our cloud provider KMS and bound to the tenant via IAM policies. Data-at-rest on host volumes uses envelope encryption; customer data keys are never shared between tenants. We support customer-managed keys (CMKs) and HSM-backed keys for enterprise accounts and Private deployments.

5) Attestation & evidence we can provide- Redacted telemetry traces showing isolation events (request_id-scoped), architecture diagrams, SIG response mapping to control objectives, and a security attestation letter signed by our Head of Security. For customers requiring deeper assurances we offer an on-site or virtual architecture review and can provide a scoped SOC 2 bridge report excerpt under NDA.

If you want, I can paste a short sample of the telemetry fields we record (timestamp, node_id, tenant_id, request_id, event_type) for your reviewers to evaluate.

-- Marcus

Patrick — great questions. Short answers here, we'll follow up with the artifacts and a signed attestation after the call: 

- Node config: our Dedicated host AMIs have swappiness set to 0 and zswap disabled by default; we will attach the relevant sanitized snippet from the image build and a short note from Infra.
- KV eviction: the runtime triggers a synchronous flush of in-process KV shards for the affected worker (so entries are not left readable by another tenant). The GC cycle is separate but the memory is zeroed before process termination where possible; the readme we attached describes the lifecycle.
- Key material: tenant keys are never written to host disk in plaintext. For Hosted we use cloud KMS envelope keys; the unwrapped data key is held in RAM inside the process with strict lifetime (seconds to minutes) and is never persisted. For Private deployments customers can bring HSM-backed keys and we integrate such that we never receive plaintext key material.

We'll prepare: (1) redacted node config snippet, (2) a 1-page signed attestation, (3) short telemetry sample, and (4) the SIG mapping doc. Expect these within 3 business days after our architecture deep-dive. If the date you booked (2026-06-01 10:00 PT) is confirmed on your side we'll go ahead and lock the artifacts delivery timeline to that call.

Thanks — looking forward to the call.
